s: Chapter 1 describes God creating the heavens and the earth over six days. He begins with light and divides it from darkness, then makes the sky, the dry land and seas, and plants. He then makes the sun, moon and stars, the sea creatures and birds, and the land animals. On the sixth day God creates man, male and female, in his own image, gives them dominion and plants for food, and sees that everything he made is very good.

God creates the heavens and the earth and everything in them by speaking over six days, repeatedly seeing that his work is good. He divides light from darkness, makes man in his image, blesses the creatures and man, and gives plants as food. He ends by seeing that all he made is very good.

l: heavens and the earth, Genesis, Chapter 1
s: God creates the heavens and the earth in the beginning. The earth is at first formless and empty, with darkness over the deep and God's Spirit hovering over the waters.

The earth begins formless and empty, covered by waters. God gathers the waters into seas so dry land appears, and calls the dry land "earth". It yields grass, herbs and fruit trees, produces living creatures, and receives light from the lights in the sky.
God says "Let there be light," and light comes to be. God sees that it is good, divides it from the darkness, and calls it "day".
God makes an expanse in the middle of the waters to divide the waters above from the waters below, and calls it "sky". On the fourth day he sets lights in it, and on the fifth day birds fly in it.

On the third day God commands the earth to yield grass, herbs yielding seed, and fruit trees, each after its kind, and it does so. God sees that they are good, and later gives them to man and to the animals as food.

On the fourth day God makes the two great lights, the greater to rule the day and the lesser to rule the night, and also the stars. He sets them in the expanse of the sky to give light to the earth, mark seasons, days and years, and divide light from darkness.

l: sea creatures and birds, Genesis, Chapter 1
s: On the fifth day God creates the large sea creatures, every living creature in the waters, and every winged bird, each after its kind. God sees that they are good and blesses them, telling them to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the seas and the earth.

On the sixth day God has the earth produce livestock, creeping things, and animals of the earth, each after its kind, and he makes them. God sees that they are good, and gives every green herb to them for food.

God makes man in his own image, male and female, on the sixth day. God blesses them, tells them to be fruitful, multiply, fill and subdue the earth and have dominion over the fish, birds and every living thing, and gives them seed-bearing herbs and fruit trees for food.

l: creation of the world, Genesis, Chapter 1
s: The world is created in six days, each ending with "evening and morning". The days run from light, to sky, to land and plants, to sun, moon and stars, to sea creatures and birds, to land animals and man. God sees the whole as very good.

Chapter 2 recounts that the heavens and earth were finished and that God rested on the seventh day, blessing and making it holy. The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, breathed life into him, and placed him in a garden in Eden, which was watered by a river that divided into four rivers: Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel, and the Euphrates. The LORD God commanded the man to eat freely from every tree except the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, on penalty of death. Finding no suitable helper among the animals the man named, the LORD God caused the man to sleep, took one of his ribs, and made a woman, whom the man welcomed as bone of his bones and flesh of his flesh. The chapter closes with the principle that a man will join with his wife and become one flesh, and notes that the two were naked and not ashamed.

The LORD God made the earth and the heavens, formed man from the dust and breathed life into him, and planted a garden in Eden where he put the man to cultivate and keep it. He commanded the man not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, declared it not good for the man to be alone, formed the animals and brought them to the man, and then made a woman from the man's rib.

The man was formed from the dust of the ground, became a living soul, and was put in the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it. He was forbidden to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, named all the livestock, birds, and animals, found no comparable helper among them, and received the woman made from his rib, saying she was bone of his bones and flesh of his flesh.

The woman was made by the LORD God from the rib he took from the man while the man slept, and was brought to him. The man said she would be called 'woman' because she was taken out of Man; she and the man were both naked and not ashamed.

The LORD God planted the garden eastward, in Eden, with trees pleasant to see and good for food, including the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil in the middle. A river went out of Eden to water it and divided into four rivers (Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel, and the Euphrates). The LORD God put the man there to cultivate and keep it.

l: tree of the knowledge of good and evil, Genesis, Chapter 2
s: This tree was one of the trees the LORD God made grow in the garden, standing in the middle along with the tree of life. The LORD God forbade the man to eat from it, saying that in the day he ate of it he would surely die.
On the seventh day God finished his work and rested from all he had done. God blessed the seventh day and made it holy because he rested in it from all his work of creation.
